narrative.overview:
A game HUD a household actually uses every day. The room is dark: near-black slate boards, one-pixel ink borders, flat fills, an inset hairline catching light along the top of every panel. The reward layer is where color lives — a saturated profession accent tints a card, gold ranks and numbers sit in a serif face, a progress bar fills in the green of a daily streak. Nothing glows, nothing gradients, nothing floats.

The game register is carried by structure and color semantics, not by novelty: accent edges, rank badges, progress bars, XP numerals, and emoji confined to the navigation and celebration moments. The professional register is carried by discipline: one column, one accent per panel, one serif, tabular numbers, and motion capped at a quarter-second unless it is a bar filling. Fun is allowed to be loud in hue; it is never allowed to be sloppy in spacing or alignment.
keyCharacteristics: Dark slate surfaces (#101218–#454e63), flat, no gradients or glows
One saturated accent per panel, assigned with a --accent custom property
Iowan Old Style serif for names, headings and every number that matters
0.6rem cards with 1px ink borders and an inset 1px top highlight
Game signals: 3px accent edges, rank badges, progress bars, tier colors
Mobile-first single column (max 42rem), six-tab bottom navigation

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: A surface carries exactly one accent. Set it with --accent (accentStyle(color)); tints and borders derive from it with color-mix. Two accents in one panel is a bug, not a flourish.

rules.name: The Ledger Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold is reserved for what the player earned: numbers, ranks, levels, currency, the active tab. Gold is never a background for body copy.

rules.name: The Flat Color Rule
rules.body: No gradients, no glows, no glassmorphism. The game energy comes from saturated hues on flat ground — the Melvor-idle discipline, not neon.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Stats Rule
rules.body: If it is a number the player earned, it is set in the display serif with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. If it is a sentence, it is set in the sans.

rules.name: The Quiet Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy is never serif and never uppercase. Uppercase is reserved for the tracked eyebrow label.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Depth is a lightness step plus a hairline. If a surface seems to float, it is wrong; lower its fill instead of adding a shadow.

dos: Do assign color through --accent per panel, so tints, borders and edges all derive from one hue.
Do set earned numbers in the display serif with tabular figures, gold when they are ranks or currency.
Do convey depth with one lightness step plus a 1px hairline, and the inset top highlight on panels.
Do keep game color semantic: green = gathering/health/goal, amber = artisan/streak/coin, violet = support/talent, red = combat/damage, blue = arcane/primary.
Do keep emoji functional — navigation icons and celebration cues only.
Do cap decorative transitions at 0.25s; bars may animate to 0.4s.
donts: Don't add gradients, glows, colored drop shadows, or glassmorphism. The energy budget is hue, not light.
Don't put two accent edges on one card (top stripe plus left border) or two accent hues in one panel.
Don't use gold as a fill behind body text or as a generic hover color.
Don't set body copy in the serif, or uppercase anything except the tracked eyebrow label.
Don't introduce a second display family, a mascot, or a cartoon illustration style; the game reads as a ledger, not a nursery.
Don't replace the flat 1px border language with Material-style elevation cards.
